trajectory_summary: The call opens with the customer venting frustration but volunteering a genuine engineer's curiosity about solar technology, along with three distinct objections (financing structure, slate roof, stale research). The rep never tests any of them and offers to remove the customer from the call list within roughly ninety seconds of first contact. The call ends amicably but with zero qualification data gathered and no attempt to re-open the door the customer himself left ajar.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown, but this should not be read as a clean, worked disqualification. The customer never had his roof claim verified, his bill was never asked about, and his own stated interest in solar technology (00:22, 01:39) was never explored. This is an unworked opt-out, not a qualified DQ — the rep exited on the customer's self-assessment rather than testing any of qualifiers.credit_qualifier, verify.roof_type_age, or verify.average_bill before conceding.

observed_outcome.quote: Totally. Well, here, I can just take you off my list here, Charles.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The call ends with the rep voluntarily removing the customer from the call list rather than any appointment being booked, tentative, or a scheduled callback; no verify-section items were completed and no next step was set.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked the interest question, but the customer volunteered a clear reason (engineering curiosity about alternate energy) unprompted at 00:22; the rep did not reference or build on this reason at any later point in the call, instead treating the customer's follow-on complaints as grounds to disengage.

script_coverage.quote: Hi. This is Meg. I'm with ION reaching out about the solar form you filled out online.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: single-angle concession on a multi-part objection
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Totally. Well, here, I can just take you off my list here, Charles.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep three separate openings (a bill number, a repeated request for current tech info, and a self-declared engineering curiosity) inside 90 seconds, and the rep tested none of them before offering to end contact. This is the clearest, most consequential gap on the call — the manager should replay the 00:22 to 01:52 stretch and walk through where each opening could have been picked up.

key_moments.quote: Pretty good. But I think you guys did pretty did a pretty good job of tricking me into, clicking one too many times.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer is questioning the legitimacy of how his info was captured, essentially a soft version of the how-did-you-get-my-number concern. The rep never explicitly re-anchors the legitimacy of the form/lead source with honest specificity; he moves straight into disqualifying the interest instead of addressing the trust question.

key_moments.quote: All I wanted to do I'm an engineer, so I love reading about, you know, alternate sources of energy and stuff like that.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a genuine, self-disclosed interest in solar technology from a technically literate customer — exactly the kind of curiosity that could be redirected toward 'let's get you real numbers for your home' rather than treated as noise ahead of a complaint.

key_moments.quote: Mhmm. And so you're gonna pay a 150, $200 a month, which is, you know, what I pay in electricity now, which it it so it doesn't test the common sense test.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a textbook objection_inversion trigger: the customer states his current bill (150-200/month) as the reason solar doesn't make sense, when that same bill is the standard justification for switching. The rep never flips this — no acknowledgment of the number, no reframing that the same money is already being spent to the utility.

key_moments.quote: And so, again, it was five years, so I thought I was clicking on getting the latest on technology about solar panels, that I could read about.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer restates, a second time, that his research is five years stale and that he wanted current information — practically inviting the rep to offer an updated look. The rep does not pick this up before moving to remove him from the list fifteen seconds later.
